cf.title: Collect ALTER PUBLICATION commands for event triggers

input.subject: Collect ALTER PUBLICATION commands for event triggers

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: message #2 notes the documentation expects a ddl_command_end entry for the main command after sql_drop. Three fixable design points remain. The patches do not state whether a row means the command ran or the catalog changed (standards-compat-2). The v2 commit messages still plan a back-patch that changes output in minor releases (standards-compat-1). Per-path collection can miss future subcommands (maintenance-fit-1).

brief.title: Report ALTER PUBLICATION drops and SET ALL in pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands()
brief.problem: Some ALTER PUBLICATION forms fire ddl_command_end, but pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() returns no entry for them. This affects DROP TABLE, DROP TABLES IN SCHEMA, SET forms that only remove members, and SET ALL TABLES or SET ALL SEQUENCES. Event trigger users who audit or deparse commands miss these commands.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 collects the publication itself as the ALTER PUBLICATION command when the command removes table or schema members, and keeps the existing per-member entries for additions. 0002 makes AlterPublicationAllFlags() report whether the publication state changed, and collects the publication when it did. 0003 calls the post-alter object access hook for SET ALL.
user_visible_surface: pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() returns a publication-level ALTER PUBLICATION row for DROP TABLE, DROP TABLES IN SCHEMA and remove-only SET.
pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() returns a row for SET ALL TABLES and SET ALL SEQUENCES when the publication state changes.
SET with both additions and removals, and SET ALL TABLES ... EXCEPT, now return a publication row plus the per-member rows.
Object access hooks now get a post-alter call for ALTER PUBLICATION SET ALL (0003).
author_claims: The missing entry is a bug, since ddl_command_end fires but reports no command.
The extra publication row next to per-member rows is intentional, as each covers a different part of the command.
0001 should go to all supported branches, or only to master if the behaviour change is too risky.
0002 and 0003 should go back to v19, where SET ALL TABLES and SET ALL SEQUENCES appeared.
Command-level auditing needs the entry even when sql_drop gives enough data to deparse.
brief.thread_state: Ian Barwick and Chao Li find v2 reasonable, and Zhijie Hou supports 0002 but asks what 0001 adds beyond sql_drop. shihao zhong measured that no-op commands still return zero rows and asks for a fixed 0002 commit message and a rebase; the author has not replied.
unclear: Whether ddl_command_end should report the command when it ran or only when the catalog changed; the patches use the second rule for some forms only.
Whether a no-op SET TABLE or SET ALL TABLES should return a row, as shihao zhong's measurements show it does not.
Whether existing event trigger users break when SET starts to return an extra row in back branches.
Whether 0003 should be committed apart from 0001 and 0002, as shihao zhong asks.
Whether the documentation on event triggers needs a change; no documentation hunk is attached.

objections.title: Row is reported only when the catalog changed, unlike other ALTER forms
objections.failure_scenario: An auditor relies on the new rows to log every ALTER PUBLICATION that ran. ALTER PUBLICATION p SET (publish='insert') returns a row every time, but a repeated SET TABLE with the same set or SET ALL TABLES on an all-tables publication returns none. The audit log misses these commands, and the gap shows up only during a review of the log.
objections.argument: Message #10 measured both rules on the same command. The author's stated goal in message #7 is command-level auditing, and that goal needs a row whenever ddl_command_end fires. The 0002 commit message says it fixes the case of no entry, but the no-op SET ALL case still returns no entry. The proposal does not state which rule ddl_command_end follows, and it attaches no documentation hunk that says so.
objections.author_must_show: Should pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() return a row for every ALTER PUBLICATION that fires ddl_command_end, and if not, where is the catalog-changed rule documented?

critic.reasoning: Message #10 measured that SET (publish=...) returns a row every time while no-op SET TABLE and SET ALL TABLES return none. The author has not replied, and no patch states which rule applies.

objections.title: Back-patching 0001 changes event trigger output in minor releases
objections.failure_scenario: A site runs an event trigger that rebuilds commands from the rows of pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands(), for example to replay DDL elsewhere. After a minor upgrade, ALTER PUBLICATION p SET TABLE with both additions and removals returns an extra publication row. The tool replays or logs the command twice, and the site finds out when the replica or audit log diverges.
objections.argument: The v2 commit messages still say 0001 goes to all supported versions and 0002 to v19. In message #2, Barwick said this kind of behaviour change usually does not get back-patched when nobody has complained. The author agreed in message #5 but did not change the plan. Zhijie Hou notes in message #4 that sql_drop already lets tools deparse the drop forms, so existing tools may already handle these cases.
objections.author_must_show: Which existing event trigger users need the drop-form row in back branches, and why is a master-only change for 0001 not enough?

critic.reasoning: The v2 commit message for 0001 still says "Backpatch to all supported versions", although the author accepted Barwick's point in message #5. The extra publication row for mixed SET is a real output change in a minor release.

objections.title: Per-path change detection leaves future ALTER PUBLICATION forms easy to miss
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new ALTER PUBLICATION subcommand and its author does not add a collection call for that path. No regression test fails. Audit triggers again see ddl_command_end with no row, and users find out only when an audit gap is reported.
objections.argument: 0001 and 0002 add collection inside each code path that changes state. AlterPublicationAllFlags() also has to report whether anything changed. The v19 SET ALL feature already missed both the collection and the post-alter hook (0002, 0003; message #3), so this per-path pattern has been missed once before. Collecting the publication once per command would also remove the split shihao zhong measured, where no-op SET ALL TABLES returns zero rows and a no-op SET (publish=...) returns a row (message #10).
objections.author_must_show: Why not collect the publication once for every ALTER PUBLICATION, so a new subcommand cannot silently skip event trigger reporting?

critic.reasoning: Per-path collection is the existing practice for ALTER PUBLICATION, so the patch did not create the pattern. But v19 SET ALL already missed both the collection and the hook, and the proposal does not say why one collection per command was not chosen.

refuted.title: Back-patching 0001 changes event trigger output in a minor release
refuted.failure_scenario: A site runs an event trigger that forwards each pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() row to other nodes or to an audit store. After a minor update, ALTER PUBLICATION ... SET with both additions and removals returns an extra publication-level row. The tool forwards or counts it as a separate command, and nodes on different minor versions record different command streams for the same DDL.
refuted.argument: The v2 commit messages still say "Backpatch to all supported versions" for 0001 and "Backpatch to v19" for 0002, which means 0002 lands in a released branch too. Message #2 notes that nobody has reported this problem and that behaviour changes like this usually stay in master. Message #5 accepts that point, but the patches were not changed. Message #4 says sql_drop already gives deparsing tools enough data for the drop forms, so the cost in back branches falls on users who parse these rows, with no reported user asking for the change.
refuted.author_must_show: Which reported user problem justifies changing the rows pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() returns in minor releases, compared with a master-only fix?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Its added point on 0002 is weaker, because message #4 says SET ALL has no other means of deparsing, which supports a fix in v19.

refuted.title: 0001 repeats what sql_drop already reports for publication member removals
refuted.failure_scenario: A tool rebuilds ALTER PUBLICATION ... DROP TABLE from sql_drop rows and also reads pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands(). After a minor update with 0001, the same command also returns a publication row, so the tool may emit the change twice or fail on the new row shape. Users notice only when replay or audit output goes wrong.
refuted.argument: For drop-only forms, sql_drop with pg_event_trigger_dropped_objects() already identifies each removed publication relation, and ddl_command_end already fires with TG_TAG 'ALTER PUBLICATION'. Message #4 asks what 0001 adds beyond this. Message #7 answers with consistency for command-level auditing, which makes it more convenient but does not show that something cannot be done today. Message #2 notes that nobody has complained, and the change still alters output in back branches.
refuted.author_must_show: Which audit or deparse task cannot be done today with sql_drop rows plus TG_TAG in ddl_command_end, and does that justify changing output in back branches?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 shows the documentation expects a ddl_command_end entry for the main command after sql_drop, as ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN gives, so 0001 restores existing practice. The back-branch risk is a duplicate of standards-compat-1.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0003 adds a post-alter object access hook call for SET ALL, and extensions read the rows of pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands().

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: Back-patching 0001 changes event trigger output in minor releases

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: 0003 makes ALTER PUBLICATION SET ALL visible to object access hook users such as sepgsql.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001 targets all supported branches, 0002 and 0003 target v19, and mixed SET returns an extra row.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each ALTER PUBLICATION code path must collect the command itself, and v19 SET ALL already missed it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands() return a row for every ALTER PUBLICATION that fires ddl_command_end, including a no-op SET TABLE or SET ALL TABLES, or only when the catalog changed?
Why not collect the publication once per ALTER PUBLICATION command, so a new subcommand cannot skip event trigger reporting?
Which existing event trigger users need the drop-form row in back branches, and why is a master-only change for 0001 not enough?
How should a trigger that reads both the publication row and the per-member rows of a mixed SET avoid counting the command twice?
Does the event trigger documentation need a change to state the rule, and can 0003 be committed apart from 0001 and 0002?

committability.owner_note: The maintenance-fit review notes that a committer in the area wrote the patch; the owner needs to know event trigger command collection and publicationcmds.c.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the rows ALTER PUBLICATION returns to event triggers, in every branch that gets the patch. If back-patched, that includes any breakage of tools that parse these rows after a minor update.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 in message #5 and answered the sql_drop question in message #7, but has not yet replied to the measurements in message #10.

priority.reason: The patches touch one backend file plus the event_trigger regression test and fix a mismatch with documented behaviour. The users are event trigger and object access hook consumers of publication DDL, and the open points are a reporting rule and the back-patch range.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check how 0001 detects removals, how AlterPublicationAllFlags() decides the state changed, or whether mixed SET can return duplicate publication rows. Only 3 of 11 messages were read directly.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add new wait event to XactLockTableWait
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a wait event, first WAIT_EVENT_XACT_DONE and later WAIT_EVENT_XACT_COMPLETE, which XactLockTableWait() and ConditionalXactLockTableWait() report during their pg_usleep() calls. Backends in these waits, for example while creating a logical replication slot on a busy system, then show a wait event in pg_stat_activity instead of NULL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Fujii Masao and Dilip Kumar approved v3, the author marked it Ready for Committer, and Fujii Masao said he would commit it once v19 development opened. No objection appears, and the thread ends in June 2025 while the entry was withdrawn in March 2026.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop."
Reverted commit(s): pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 74ac377d75135e02064fc4427bec401277b4f60c.

The previous change contained a misconception about how publications
are cleaned up on the subscriber. The newly added log message could
confuse users, particularly when running pg_createsubscriber with
--dry-run - users would see a "dropping publication" message
immediately followed by a "no publications found" message.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize walsender handling invalid messages of 'drop publication'
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how walsender handles invalidation messages from 'drop publication' on releases before PG 14, which lack the XLOG_XACT_INVALIDATIONS record type. pgoutput stops doing needless cache invalidation, and a relid-to-relfilenode hash map replaces a hash sequential search; the patch targets REL_13_STABLE and back branches only.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one reviewed the patch for four months. Andres Freund then objected that users hitting the issue should upgrade, and that performance improvements are rarely backpatched, and not when they would go only into back branches without first maturing in the development branch. The author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's one thing to decide to backpatch an
optimization if it had time to "mature" in the development branch, but from
what I undestand you're proposing to apply this just to the back branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add accumulated statistics for wait event
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Daniel Gustafsson
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch records, per backend and per wait event, the number of waits and the accumulated wait time, so the counts survive after the wait ends and appear in a view such as pg_stat_waitaccum. Later versions keep these statistics in a hash table and add a track_wait_timing setting to turn the timing part on and off.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying to HEAD. The author said there was no time to rebase it in that commitfest, so the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, Michael Paquier argued that client-side sampling of pg_stat_activity finds bottlenecks at lower cost than server-side counters for all backends. Benchmarks showed up to about 10% overhead in read-only tests, and Kyotaro Horiguchi found frequent hash lookups even with timing off.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since the thread has stalled and there is no updated
patch I've marked this entry Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zheng Li (zhengli), Zhijie Hou (houzj), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), vigneshwaran C (vignesh.postgres), Runqi Tian (runqitian)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replicate DDL commands through logical replication so that schema changes reach subscribers, for example during major version upgrades. The later patch set deparses DDL commands in event triggers into a JSON format string, WAL-logs it, and the apply worker rebuilds and runs the command, starting with create, alter and drop table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.

precedents_retrieved.title: Xact event callback at command start
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a way for an extension to run code before each SQL statement in a transaction, so that it can implement server-side statement-level rollback. Early versions used hooks around start_xact_command(), later versions used a new XACT_EVENT_COMMAND_START event for xact callbacks, and v5 went back to a hook called after start_xact_command().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Tom Lane objected to exposing an API for statement-level rollback in an extension, because top-level transaction state is tied to backend internals and the hook placements would be fragile and add overhead to the exec_* functions in postgres.c. Andres Freund added that a real solution needs core work, such as making subtransactions cheap enough to avoid xid wraparound, and that these hooks do not move toward it. Tom Lane also said the new xact callback events were the wrong design, since they broke postgres_fdw. After this, the author said there was no chance of inclusion and offered to withdraw the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm *very* unconvinced it makes sense to implement a feature like this in an extension / that we should expose API for that purpose. To me the top-level transaction state is way too tied to our internals for it to be reasonably dealt with in an extension.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix NULL dereference in pg_get_database_ddl()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a NULL check in pg_get_database_ddl_internal() so that a dattablespace pointing to a missing tablespace no longer crashes the backend in pg_strcasecmp(). In that case the function omits the TABLESPACE clause, and a regression test covers it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only reproducer was a manual update of pg_database with allow_system_table_mods, and David Rowley asked why this self-inflicted catalog corruption should matter more than other such cases. The author then found no supported path to the state, because the catalog snapshot keeps both lookups consistent and DROP TABLESPACE fails while the database directory exists, so he withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Can you explain why this method of self-inflicted catalogue corruption
is any more important than any of the just-about-infinite other ways
there are of causing issues by manually updating the catalogue tables?

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: add \si, \sm, \st and \sr functions to show CREATE commands for indexes, matviews, triggers and tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql commands \si, \sm, \st and \sr that show the CREATE command for indexes, materialized views, triggers and tables, modelled on the existing \sf and \sv. Indexes and triggers use pg_get_triggerdef() and pg_indexes.indexdef, while psql rebuilds table and materialized view DDL itself with its own client-side queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the output must be fully correct DDL, so psql would need a second copy of pg_dump's large and often-changing DDL logic. He said a shared library built from pg_dump's code should come first. He also noted that the patch fails on older servers, which describe.c must support, and that the commands need review against CVE-2018-1058-style search_path attacks. The author did not respond, and the entry was marked returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I can't accept that we want another copy in psql --- especially one that looks nothing like what pg_dump has.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert refactoring of restore command code to shell_restore.c
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commits 24c35ec and 57169ad.  PreRestoreCommand() and
PostRestoreCommand() need to be put closer to the system() call calling
a restore_command, as they enable in_restore_command for the startup
process which would in turn trigger an immediate proc_exit() in the
SIGTERM handler.  Perhaps we could get rid of this behavior entirely,
but 24c35ec has made the window where the flag is enabled much larger
than it was, and any Postgres-like actions (palloc, etc.) taken by code
paths while the flag is enabled could lead to more severe issues in the
shutdown processing.

Note that curculio has showed that there are much more problems in this
area, unrelated to this change, actually, hence the issues related to
that had better be addressed first.  Keeping the code of HEAD in line
with the stable branches should make that a bit easier.

Per discussion with Andres Freund and Nathan Bossart.

precedents_retrieved.title: Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Relax transactional restrictions on ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE (redux).
Reverted commit(s): Revert to 9.6 treatment of ALTER TYPE enumtype ADD VALUE.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Originally committed as 15bc038f (plus some follow-ups), this was
reverted in 28e07270 due to a problem discovered in parallel
workers.  This new version corrects that problem by sending the
list of uncommitted enum values to parallel workers.

Here follows the original commit message describing the change:

To prevent possibly breaking indexes on enum columns, we must keep
uncommitted enum values from getting stored in tables, unless we
can be sure that any such column is new in the current transaction.

Formerly, we enforced this by disallowing ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE
from being executed at all in a transaction block, unless the target
enum type had been created in the current transaction.  This patch
removes that restriction, and instead insists that an uncommitted enum
value can't be referenced unless it belongs to an enum type created
in the same transaction as the value.  Per discussion, this should be
a bit less onerous.  It does require each function that could possibly
return a new enum value to SQL operations to check this restriction,
but there aren't so many of those that this seems unmaintainable.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P8] is about replicating DDL through a hand-written deparser and was withdrawn over that deparser's long-term maintenance cost. This proposal adds no deparser and does not touch parse node structures, so that reason does not apply. No thread message points to an earlier discussion of collecting ALTER PUBLICATION for event triggers; message #3 only names the commit that added SET ALL.
Two objections raised. 0003, the post-alter hook call, follows the existing practice of AlterPublicationOptions() and raises no compatibility concern.

The patches add no WAL records, catalog columns, on-disk format changes or protocol messages, so there is nothing for pg_upgrade or a standby to handle. The only cross-node effect is through user tools that forward event trigger output, covered above.

The patches add no new privilege or exposure. Event triggers still need superuser or a role allowed to create them, the new rows describe a publication that the session's role already altered, and 0003 closes a gap for object access hooks such as sepgsql instead of opening one.
Nothing else from this angle. There is no hot-path cost, no new dependency and no fit problem, and a committer in the area wrote the patch. [P8] is about the DDL deparser and does not apply here.
No existing mechanism covers 0002 or 0003. Message #4 confirms that nothing reports SET ALL today, and the post-alter hook has no substitute.

No demand objection. The patches fix a mismatch with documented behaviour: message #2 notes the docs say sql_drop is followed by a ddl_command_end entry for the main command. The cost falls on event trigger users, and message #4 says SET ALL has no other way to be deparsed. The lack of field reports in message #2 bears on backpatching 0001, which is not a demand question.
